intro: A predicted noise vector lets a diffusion sampler estimate the clean signal. A deterministic DDIM step recombines that estimate and the same noise direction at an earlier, cleaner noise level.
task: Recover the predicted clean sample and calculate one eta-zero DDIM update. Check the identity step and the clean endpoint before trying an intermediate noise level.
requirements: sample and predicted_noise are nonempty arrays of the same shape with at least one dimension. The scalar cumulative retentions satisfy 1e-12<=alpha_bar<=previous_alpha_bar<=1.

Return a dictionary with sample=previous and predicted_clean=clean. These alpha values are cumulative retentions, not per-step beta or alpha values. This is deterministic eta=0 without clipping, random noise or a trained denoiser.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Use the forward equation in reverse
Check the two boundaries
hints.body: Equal retentions should preserve the sample. previous_alpha_bar=1 should return the predicted clean value.

explanation: The earlier diffusion state has at least as much retained signal as the current state. Reversing that ordering would move toward more noise, outside this lesson’s update contract.
An exact predicted noise reconstructs the clean signal used in a synthetic forward process. A real denoiser can be wrong; the formula does not guarantee clean predictions.
Ported the upstream eta-zero DDIM equation and exposed its clean estimate alongside the previous sample. Added an explicit positive retention floor and direction checks.
